subject: Week 33: gift-debris sweep — button batteries are the top hazard
bodyText:
This week
Avi hits day 229 in peak holiday mode: expect long babble strings ("mamamama," "bababababa") — a CDC 9-month checkpoint item — plus raking food with his fingers and hunting for objects you hide. Many babies crawl in this stretch, though the CDC dropped crawling from its checklist entirely — some skip it and go straight to pulling to stand, which is emerging for early movers (CDC checkpoint: 12 months). Stranger anxiety runs at full strength through 7-10 months, so expect clinginess with rotating holiday visitors.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Clinginess and one-parent preference around holiday visitors — stranger anxiety peaks 7-10 months; give him warm-up time in your arms before hand-offs.
- [low concern] Sleep disruption for 1-3 nights around travel or late gatherings — protect the usual bedtime where you can.
- [monitor] Upper-respiratory cluster after extended-family contact — track fever, feeding, and breathing effort rather than counting days.
- [call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving, or any new wheezing.
- [call now] Suspected button-battery or magnet ingestion from new toys or gift debris — ER immediately, do not wait for symptoms; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Run a floor-level sweep before and after gift-opening: ribbons, coin batteries, small ornaments, and loose battery compartments on new toys are the season's ingestion hazards. AAP: Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Put raking-size finger foods on the tray daily — puffs, banana pieces, well-cooked lentils. Raking is the CDC 9-month item; the two-finger pincer it feeds is checked at 12 months. Featuring iron-rich options now also sets up the hemoglobin rescreen at the 9-month visit. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Answer his babble strings as conversation — pause, respond, wait for the return serve. Conversational turns, not word count alone, predict language-network development (Romeo et al. 2018). Romeo et al. 2018 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Cap the schedule at one major event per day and hold naps fixed — an overtired evening collapse costs more than any gathering delivers. AAP: Baby Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 235 (Jan 1, 2027): New Year's — he will be asleep at midnight; keep bedtime and log it as a parents-only marker.
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — book it now for early in the window; iron rescreen, influenza #2 if first season, and possibly an ASQ-3 developmental screen.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses fingers to 'rake' food toward herself
  AAP window: day 210-270
  What to look for: Pre-pincer grasp. Coincides with starting finger foods.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-fingers-rake/complete

- Crawls on hands and knees, or scoots
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Some babies skip crawling and go straight to cruising — that is within normal range.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/crawls/complete

- Moves from sitting into a crawl or lie-down position
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Postural transition. Predicts comfortable independent exploration.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/gets-from-sit-to-crawl/complete

- Cries or protests when a parent leaves the room
  AAP window: day 210-365
  What to look for: Peak separation anxiety. Healthy attachment, even when it makes drop-off hard.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/cries-when-parent-leaves/complete

- Catches himself with his arms when tipping over while sitting
  AAP window: day 210-300
  What to look for: Protective arm extension — reaching out to break a sideways or forward topple. Makes independent sitting safe enough for hands-busy play.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/catches-self-when-sitting/complete
